market_title: Average auction price has doubled since 2013: ₹1.7 Cr per buy then, ₹3.5 Cr at the 2025 mega auction
market_sowhat: Budget about 2× the 2013 price for the same buy at a mega auction (1.6× at the 2026 mini auction); 2025–26 bids averaged 245% above base price.
franchise_title: 2026: RR got 1.63× fair value from ₹34 Cr of buys; PBKS spent the most (₹108 Cr) for 0.72×
franchise_sowhat: Over 2013–2026, CSK (1.19) and RR (1.14) run the most efficient auctions. Spend is unrelated to win % (r = −0.03); Value Index is not (r = +0.35). Buy output per crore, not names.
valuemap_title: 2026: 24 steals delivered above-median impact at below-median prices; 8 buys were overpaid
valuemap_sowhat: Keep the Steals and Stars; Overpaid and Passenger buys are the release shortlist before the next auction.
steals_title: 2026: ₹0.3 Cr Kartik Tyagi returned 34× fair value while ₹27 Cr Rishabh Pant was overpaid by ₹19.5 Cr
steals_sowhat: Every one of the five most overpaid 2026 players cost ₹14 Cr or more; the best value sat in ₹30-lakh buys. Open the demo here.
roles_title: 2026: overseas buys cost 2.4× as much as Indian buys but returned less per crore (0.88 vs 1.11)
roles_sowhat: Across 2013–2026 Indian bowlers are the best-value role (1.22) and overseas bowlers the worst (0.84): spend overseas slots only on proven match-winners.
brackets_title: 2026: buys under ₹2 Cr returned 2.7–3.5× fair value per crore; ₹10 Cr+ signings returned 0.55×
brackets_sowhat: It holds across 2013–2026 (base-price 4.1× vs ₹10 Cr+ 0.49×). Marquee buys beat median impact 88% of the time, but each crore buys far more output in the cheap brackets.
matched_text: 99.0% of auction spend (₹3,237 of ₹3,269 Cr) is matched to a Cricsheet player; most of the 66 unmatched buys never played an IPL match.
